diagnosis.root_cause: Q16 scans 8M partsupp rows single-threaded using unordered_map<Key, unordered_set<int32_t>> for distinct supplier counting. Hash operations on nested containers cause heavy heap allocation and cache misses. No parallelism despite 64 available cores.
diagnosis.memory_footprint: unordered_set per group: ~2000 groups x avg 50 suppliers x 40B/node = ~4MB scattered heap; unordered_map overhead ~2000 x 56B = 112KB

edit_summary: Parallelized Q16 partsupp scan with OpenMP (64 threads). Replaced unordered_set<int> target_sizes and excluded_types with O(1) lookup arrays. Replaced per-group unordered_set<int32_t> for distinct suppkeys with bitsets (100K bits = 12.5KB each) merged via bitwise OR across threads. Pre-classified parts to avoid repeated dictionary lookups.
expected_improvement: ~95% reduction in fused_scan_partsupp latency (630ms -> ~20-30ms) from 64-way parallelism + elimination of hash container overhead. Net batch improvement ~30% (600ms savings on 2037ms total).
